node.title: Biotechnology and its Applications: Application of biotechnology in agriculture – tissue

questions.stem: In plant tissue culture, the piece of plant tissue used to initiate the culture is called the
questions.explanation: An explant is the small piece of living tissue, such as a leaf, stem or meristem part, that is placed on a nutrient medium to start a culture. The callus is the mass of undifferentiated cells formed from it.

optionRationale.1: A scion is the shoot used in grafting.
optionRationale.3: A callus is the cell mass formed after culturing, not the starting tissue.
optionRationale.4: A protoplast is a cell stripped of its wall.

questions.stem: Bt cotton has been made resistant to
questions.explanation: Bt cotton carries the cry genes of Bacillus thuringiensis, which make the insecticidal Cry protein. This protein protects the plant against cotton bollworms, which are major insect pests of cotton.

optionRationale.1: Bt toxin does not act on fungi.
optionRationale.2: Nematode resistance was achieved in tobacco using RNA interference.
optionRationale.4: Bt cotton is not a drought-tolerant crop.

questions.objective: State the pest controlled by Bt cotton

questions.stem: Genetically modified organisms are those whose
options: genes have been altered by manipulation
phenotype has changed only by selective breeding
chromosome number was halved by colchicine
genes were silenced by natural mutation
questions.explanation: Plants, bacteria, fungi and animals whose genes have been altered by manipulation are called genetically modified organisms. The alteration is usually done by rDNA technology, for example by the insertion of a foreign gene into the host.

optionRationale.2: Selective breeding is a conventional method and not genetic manipulation.
optionRationale.3: Colchicine is used to double, not halve, chromosome number.
optionRationale.4: Natural mutation is not deliberate manipulation of genes.

questions.stem: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) is based on the principle of
options: hybridisation of a labelled DNA probe
separation of molecules by density-gradient centrifugation
questions.explanation: ELISA detects the presence of an antigen, or antibodies against a pathogen, through the specific antigen-antibody reaction. A positive result shows infection by the pathogen, so it is used in molecular diagnosis.

optionRationale.1: Hybridisation of a probe is used in DNA-based detection, not in ELISA.
optionRationale.2: Restriction digestion is used to cut DNA.
optionRationale.3: Density-gradient centrifugation is not the basis of this test.

questions.stem: The gene cryIAb of Bacillus thuringiensis is used to control
questions.explanation: The Cry proteins are coded by cry genes, and each is toxic to a particular group of insects. The gene cryIAb controls the corn borer, while cryIAc and cryIIAb control cotton bollworms.

optionRationale.2: Nematodes are controlled by RNA interference, not by this gene.
optionRationale.3: Cry proteins are insecticidal and not antifungal.
optionRationale.4: The gene cryIAb is used for the corn borer, not for aphids.

questions.objective: Match cry genes with target pests

questions.stem: Transgenic mice are being developed to test the safety of the
questions.explanation: Transgenic mice are developed to test the safety of the polio vaccine before it is used on humans. If found reliable and accurate, they can replace the use of monkeys for testing vaccine batches.

optionRationale.2: The textbook example is the polio vaccine.
optionRationale.3: The textbook example is the polio vaccine, not BCG.
optionRationale.4: The textbook example is the polio vaccine, not typhoid.

questions.objective: State a use of transgenic animals in vaccine testing

questions.stem: Gene therapy is a method of treating a hereditary disease by
options: injecting the patient with the missing enzyme repeatedly
giving antibiotics to kill the defective cells
delivering a normal gene into the cells to compensate for the defective one
questions.explanation: Gene therapy is a collection of methods that corrects a gene defect diagnosed in a child or embryo. Normal genes are inserted into the individual's cells and tissues to take over the function of the non-functional gene.

optionRationale.1: Repeated enzyme injection is an enzyme replacement approach and not gene therapy.
optionRationale.2: Surgery does not correct a genetic defect.
optionRationale.3: Antibiotics act on bacteria and not on genetic defects.

questions.stem: PCR can detect a pathogen earlier than ELISA in a suspected HIV patient because PCR
options: destroys the antibodies of the patient
can amplify even a very small amount of the pathogen's nucleic acid, before antibodies reach detectable levels
uses live virus as the template
questions.explanation: PCR makes many copies of the pathogen's nucleic acid, so even a very low load can be detected at an early stage. ELISA depends on the presence of antibodies or antigens, which may be low in the early phase of infection.

optionRationale.1: PCR does not act on antibodies.
optionRationale.3: PCR needs only nucleic acid as template, not live virus.
optionRationale.4: PCR needs both primers and a heat-stable DNA polymerase.

questions.objective: Explain why PCR is used for early detection

questions.stem: In tobacco plants protected from the nematode Meloidogyne incognita, the host cells made sense and antisense RNA of a nematode gene. These formed double-stranded RNA that
options: cut the tobacco DNA at specific sites
increased the translation of the nematode mRNA
silenced the specific mRNA of the nematode, so the parasite could not survive in the host
was converted into a Cry protein
questions.explanation: The introduced genes made complementary RNAs inside the host cells. Their double-stranded RNA triggered RNA interference, which silenced the nematode's specific mRNA, and so the parasite could not live in the transgenic tobacco.

optionRationale.1: Cutting DNA at specific sites is the work of restriction enzymes.
optionRationale.2: RNAi blocks translation; it does not increase it.
optionRationale.4: Cry protein comes from Bacillus thuringiensis genes, not from this RNA.

questions.objective: Explain RNA interference in nematode protection

questions.stem: Match the item in List-I with its use in List-II.
questions.explanation: Golden rice has been engineered to contain vitamin A. Bt cotton makes the Cry protein that kills bollworms. RNA interference silences a specific mRNA, and PCR amplifies DNA so that infection can be detected early.

optionRationale.1: This pairs 'Golden rice' with 'Resistant to bollworm through the Cry protein', which describes 'Bt cotton'.
optionRationale.2: This pairs 'RNA interference' with 'Amplifying DNA for early detection of a pathogen', which describes 'PCR'.
optionRationale.4: This pairs 'Golden rice' with 'Silencing of a specific mRNA', which describes 'RNA interference'.

right: I. Resistant to bollworm through the Cry protein
II. Amplifying DNA for early detection of a pathogen
IV. Silencing of a specific mRNA

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Transgenic animals can be used as models for studying human diseases.
Reason (R): Transgenic animals can be made to produce useful biological products, such as the human protein alpha-1-antitrypsin.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Transgenic animals are used as models of human diseases such as cancer, cystic fibrosis and Alzheimer's, so A is true. They are also used to make products such as alpha-1-antitrypsin, so R is true, but R does not explain A.

optionRationale.1: R is a separate use and does not explain the disease-model use.
optionRationale.4: A is true and R is true.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Plants produced by micropropagation are genetically different from the plant from which the explant was taken.
Reason (R): Micropropagated plants are somaclones, which are genetically identical to the original plant.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Micropropagation produces many plants from an explant by repeated mitotic divisions, and the resulting plants are somaclones, which are genetically identical to the parent plant. So A is false and R is true.

optionRationale.1: A is false, so both cannot be true.
optionRationale.2: A is false, so both cannot be true.
optionRationale.3: R is true, so this option is wrong.

questions.objective: State the genetic nature of micropropagated plants

questions.stem: Match the term in List-I with its meaning in List-II.
questions.explanation: Biopiracy is the unauthorised use of bio-resources. The Genetic Engineering Approval Committee judges the validity of GM research and the safety of introducing GM organisms. A patent is a right for an invention, and basmati was patented by a US company.

optionRationale.1: This pairs 'Biopiracy' with 'Body that decides on the validity and safety of GM research', which describes 'GEAC'.
optionRationale.3: This pairs 'Biopatent' with 'Rice variety patented by a US company', which describes 'Basmati'.
optionRationale.4: This pairs 'Biopiracy' with 'Right granted by a government for an invention', which describes 'Biopatent'.

questions.objective: Match ethical issues and regulation terms

right: I. Use of bio-resources by companies without proper authorisation
II. Right granted by a government for an invention
III. Rice variety patented by a US company
IV. Body that decides on the validity and safety of GM research

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about GM crops.
A. GM crops can have enhanced nutritional value.
B. GM crops can help reduce the reliance on chemical pesticides.
C. GM crops reduce the efficiency of mineral usage by plants.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Golden rice shows that GM crops can have better nutrition, and Bt crops reduce pesticide use. GM crops are made to increase, not reduce, the efficiency of mineral usage by plants, so C is wrong.

optionRationale.1: C is wrong, as GM crops increase mineral use efficiency.
optionRationale.2: C is wrong, so this option cannot be correct.
optionRationale.4: C is wrong, so not all three are correct.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on benefits of GM crops

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about transgenic animals.
A. Their DNA has been manipulated to possess and express an extra, foreign gene.
B. Over 95 per cent of all existing transgenic animals are mice.
C. They cannot be used to study how genes regulate normal physiological functions.
D. They can be designed to be more sensitive to toxic substances for toxicity testing.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: A transgenic animal expresses a foreign gene, and most of them are mice. They are also made sensitive to toxins for safety testing. They are in fact used to study how genes regulate normal functions, so C is wrong.

optionRationale.1: D is also correct, so this option is incomplete.
optionRationale.2: C is wrong, and A is correct.
optionRationale.3: C is wrong, so not all four are correct.
